what: Wayfair sells furniture and home goods online. It carries almost no inventory: suppliers ship directly to the buyer, and Wayfair runs the website, the marketing and much of the delivery for bulky items.
customers: Households in the United States, Canada, Britain and Germany furnishing a home, plus trade customers such as interior designers.
money: furniture, decor and housewares sold online
Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Germany
moat: A logistics network built for bulky goods, which parcel carriers handle badly, plus a catalogue of millions of items no physical store can hold.
risks: Still loses money: $160M of net loss on $13.2B of revenue
Revenue is below where it was in 2021 and furniture demand follows house moves, which are depressed
$4.3B of debt against $1.5B of cash, much of it convertible
opportunities: $602M of free cash flow despite the accounting loss, because the asset-light model ties up little capital
Revenue grew from $11.9B to $12.5B last year, the first growth since the pandemic
Analysts see about 36% upside, with 30 covering the stock
watch: Active customers and orders per customer, and whether free cash flow stays positive.
